texts.preamble: Mehboob Qureshi And Others ... vs State Of Uttarakhand Through Secretary ... on 16 November, 2019 Author: Alok Kumar Verma Bench: Ramesh Ranganathan, Alok Kumar Verma In The High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital Writ Petition (Ms) No. 3845 of 2018
texts.facts: The Division Bench also directed all Executive Officers of Local Self Governments, Municipal Corporations, Municipalities, Nagar Panchayats and other Panchayats to ensure that no animal is slaughtered in the public streets/public paths/roads and at open spaces, open to public gaze. 2. Pursuant to the said order dated 20.09.2018, the Haldwani slaughter house, and the other slaughter houses in the State, were all closed, evidently because they were not in compliance with the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Business) Regulations, 2011. The other direction, issued by the Division Bench in its order dated 20.09.2018, to ensure that no animal is slaughtered in streets, parks, roads and open spaces etc, has evidently not been complied with, since meat continues to be sold unabated in all hotels/restaurants in the State of Uttarakhand, and continues to be consumed by the residents of this State. Mehboob Qureshi And Others ... vs State Of Uttarakhand Through Secretary ... on 16 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38257152/ 1 3. The respondents have not only violated the order passed by the Division Bench in WPPIL No.152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018, but also the earlier order of the Division Bench in WPPIL No.77 of 2010 dated 19.12.2011, whereby the State and its agencies were required to ensure that adequate number of slaughter houses were available in the areas coming under Municipalities, and other local authorities, within a period of three years. 4. At every stage of the hearing of this case, the Handwani Municipality has expressed some difficulty or the other in complying with the directions of the Division Bench in WPPIL No. 77 and 73 of 2011 dated 19.12.2011, and in WPPIL No. 152 of 2018 dated 20.09.2018. On a few occasions when the matter was listed, the Learned Counsel for the Municipality did not even choose to be present in Court forcing us to direct the Commissioner to be present in Court, along with the entire records, to enable effective adjudication of the lis. 5. Initially the Haldwani Municipality submitted an application to the Central Authorities seeking a license to establish a slaughter house to slaughter 55 Buffalos each day. When the matter was listed, before us thereafter, they complained that permission was not forthcoming; and that their repeated requests have been rejected on one ground or the other by the Central Authorities. On the learned Counsel for the petitioner pointing out that the pre-existing slaughter house in Haldwani Municipality catered only to the slaughter of 15 to 20 Buffalos every day, and it was wholly unnecessary for the Haldwani Municipality to approach the Central Government and it would have sufficed for them to seek permission of the State Government to establish a slaughter house, for slaughter of less than 50 Buffalos every day, the Haldwani Municipality had, thereafter, made an application to the State Government.
